classification.difficultyReason: Choose the all-different complement, track the shrinking number of admissible weekdays, then remove the all-three match to isolate exactly one matching pair.

content.prompt: Three people are chosen at random and asked what day of the week they were born. Assume their birth weekdays are independent and all seven weekdays are equally likely. Find the probability that

children.label: a
children.prompt: two or three people were born on the same day of the week.

answer.worked:
Use the complement that all three birth weekdays are different. After the first person, 6 weekdays remain available for the second and 5 for the third.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least two match})&=1-1\times\frac67\times\frac57\\P(\text{at least two match})&=\frac{19}{49}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: exactly two people were born on the same day of the week.

answer.worked:
Subtract the probability that all three match from part (a). For all three to match, the second and third people must each match the first.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly two match})&=\frac{19}{49}-\frac17\times\frac17\\P(\text{exactly two match})&=\frac{18}{49}.\end{align*}$$
